title: Fugue in E-flat major
blurb: The only fugue here whose entries all stay on the tonic and the dominant.
card: A six-bar subject, so the four voices need twenty-seven bars just to state it once each.
history: The longest subject of any Book II fugue on the site: twenty notes stretched over six bars, mostly in long values. Bass first, then tenor, alto, soprano, climbing, and the exposition alone eats nearly two fifths of the piece. After that Bach stops repeating it exactly — five of the nine statements come back altered — and at bars 37 and 59 the next voice enters one bar behind the last, so a six-bar subject runs against itself for five of them.

Two bars of the C minor fugue you can hold in your ear. Six you cannot; by the time the fourth bar of a statement arrives you have usually stopped hearing it as the subject. That is the case for the brackets.

Book II was put together in Leipzig around 1739–42, nearly twenty years after Book I, out of pieces Bach had been writing over a much longer span. The main source is the London autograph in the British Library, some of it in his hand, some in Anna Magdalena's.
